loop.top3_why: Candidate A uses a weighted inverse‑error scheme on the full model pool, which is well suited to a highly predictable, trend‑dominated series with unstable model rankings across the three validation windows. Its overall validation score is the best (0.6769) and its per‑window performance is reasonably balanced, with only a modest dip in the second window. The weighted scheme mitigates the risk of over‑relying on any single model that may be unstable, aligning with the diagnosis that several models carry correlated error and that ranking stability is low.
loop.top3_why_not: Candidate B (plain mean) has a slightly higher overall score and is more stable across windows, but it does not exploit the relative performance of the models and may be less robust when the ranking changes. Candidate C has a higher overall score and more extreme per‑window values, indicating higher variance and less stability. Given the trend‑dominated nature of the series and the need for a robust combination, A is the preferred choice.
